'''Roger Steare''' is a British ethicist and corporate philosopher. He has been an Honorary Visiting Professor and Corporate Philosopher in Residence at the [[Cass Business School]], and Visiting Professor of European Studies at the [[College of Europe]]. He is the author of books on corporate ethics and a columnist for the [[Financial Times]], also working at the FT's Headspring Executive Development.

==Career==

Steare's early career included roles as a [[social work]]er and banker, and ten years as chief executive of a recruitment company.<ref name = "Smith">{{Cite news | issn = 0307-1766 | title = Roger Steare, Cass Business School | first = Emmanuelle | last = Smith | work = Financial Times | accessdate = 6 August 2012 | url = https://www.ft.com/content/fd360472-c5b6-11e1-a5d5-00144feabdc0 }}</ref>

He was Honorary Visiting Professor of Organisational Ethics, and Corporate Philosopher in Residence at the [[Cass Business School]] in London. He taught on the Executive MBA Programs as well as consulting with external corporate clients through Cass Executive Education.<ref name = "Smith" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cass.city.ac.uk/courses/executive-education/our-teaching-staff |title=Executive Education University 'One of The World Leading Executive Universities' |publisher=Cass.city.ac.uk |accessdate=17 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111118235324/http://www.cass.city.ac.uk/courses/executive-education/our-teaching-staff |archive-date=18 November 2011 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

He is also a fellow of the cross-party policy think tank, ResPublica<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.zermattsummit.org/speakers1/253-roger-steare.html |title=Roger Steare |publisher=Zermattsummit.org |accessdate=17 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120105031653/http://zermattsummit.org/speakers1/253-roger-steare.html |archive-date=5 January 2012 |df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref name="econ">{{cite web |url=http://www.econ.ihu.edu.gr/index.php/en/faculty-list/169-steare-roger.html |title=Prof Roger Steare |publisher=Econ.ihu.edu.gr |accessdate=17 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111229225633/http://www.econ.ihu.edu.gr/index.php/en/faculty-list/169-steare-roger.html |archive-date=29 December 2011 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> founded by [[Phillip Blond]] in 2009. Steare's essay on ''The Power of Love in Business'' was included in ResPublica's "Changing The Debate: The Ideas Redefining Britain".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://respublica.org.uk/item/Changing-the-Debate-The-Ideas-Redefining-Britain-dfln |title=Think Tank &#124; Phillip Blond &#124; Big Society &#124; Government policy &#124; Changing the Debate: The Ideas Redefining Britain |publisher=ResPublica |accessdate=17 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111223072425/http://www.respublica.org.uk/item/Changing-the-Debate-The-Ideas-Redefining-Britain-dfln |archive-date=23 December 2011 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

Steare was a member of the Expert Drafting Committee for [[Rights and Humanity]], invited by the British Government to prepare recommendations for the G20 London Summit in April 2009.<ref name="respublica">{{cite web |author=Professor Roger Steare |url=http://www.respublica.org.uk/author/Professor-Roger-Steare |title=Professor Roger Steare |publisher=Respublica.org.uk |accessdate=17 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120416014845/http://www.respublica.org.uk/author/Professor-Roger-Steare |archive-date=16 April 2012 |df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref name="specialistspeakers">{{cite web|url=http://www.specialistspeakers.com/?p=1961 |title=Prof Roger Steare Speaker Profile Specialist Speakers Bureau |publisher=Specialistspeakers.com |accessdate=17 December 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://bunhill.city.ac.uk/media/events.nsf/(allEvents)/6C1D556075AF7E6A8025781100541A75?OpenDocument |title=Cass Business School &#124; TANC (The Actuarial Network at Cass): Ethicability – Insights into Moral DNA |publisher=Bunhill.city.ac.uk |date=24 March 2011 |accessdate=17 December 2011}}</ref>

In collaboration with Athens-based chartered psychologist [[Pavlos Stamboulides]], Steare conducts empirical research on moral character, judgement and behaviour. Some of this research was published in [[The Times]]<ref>The Times (London), 8 October 2010, pp 56–7</ref> in October 2010, in a speech by [[Hector Sants]] of the [[Financial Services Authority]] in 2010,<ref name="Hill">{{Cite news | first = Andrew | last = Hill | issn = 0307-1766 | title = Corporate culture: Lofty aspirations | work = [[Financial Times]] | accessdate = 6 August 2012 | date = 15 July 2012 | url = https://www.ft.com/content/d1b4b71a-ccde-11e1-9960-00144feabdc0}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fsa.gov.uk/pages/Library/Communication/Speeches/2010/1004_hs.shtml |title=Can culture be regulated? |publisher=Fsa.gov.uk |date=4 October 2010 |accessdate=17 December 2011}}</ref> by [[PricewaterhouseCoopers|PwC]] UK in 2010,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.pwcwebcast.co.uk/dpliv_mu/Trust_the%20behavioural%20challenge_Oct%202010.pdf |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2011-10-27 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425112035/http://www.pwcwebcast.co.uk/dpliv_mu/Trust_the%20behavioural%20challenge_Oct%202010.pdf |archive-date=25 April 2012 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> and in ''The challenges of risk, culture, behaviour and corporate integrity in financial services''<ref>{{cite book | last=Steare|first=Roger |title=The challenges of risk, culture, behaviour and corporate integrity in financial services |url=http://www.ey.com/Publication/vwLUAssets/EY-moral-dna-in-fs/$FILE/EY-moral-dna-in-fs.pdf |publisher=[[Ernst & Young|EY]] |year=2017}}</ref> for [[Ernst & Young|EY]] in 2017. He is co-designer of the [[psychometric profile]] ''MoralDNA'', used to measure moral values.<ref name = "Smith" />

Steare is the author of ''Ethicability'', first published in 2006 and now in its 5th edition,<ref name="RRB">{{cite web|url=http://www.thecorporatephilosopher.org/book/|title=Read Roger's Books |website=The Corporate Philosopher |accessdate=18 March 2020}}</ref> and of ''Thinking Outside the Inbox'', published in 2019.<ref name="RRB" /> He is a regular contributor to Chartered Banker<ref>[http://www.charteredbanker.com/MainWebSite/Resources/Document/magazineapril11-%20loveisintheair.pdf] {{dead link|date=February 2018}}</ref> magazine in which he challenges the "dysfunctional totalitarian construct" of modern corporations,<ref>{{cite news |work=Financial Times |date=14 February 2011 |title=Comment, "Workplace itself is a totalitarian plutocratic state"}}</ref> In July 2020, he became a columnist for the [[Financial Times]].<ref name="FT-2020-07">{{cite news |title=Safety at work goes beyond pandemic worries |url=https://on.ft.com/2DaJgTQ |accessdate=18 September 2020 |work=[[Financial Times]] |date=27 July 2020}}</ref>

On 22 July 2012, he was a guest on the [[BBC World Service]]'s "In the Balance" programme, in an episode entitled ''Holding Companies to Account''.<ref>{{Cite episode  | title = Holding Companies to Account | series = In the Balance | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/iplayer/episode/p00vjqvt/In_the_Balance_Holding_Companies_to_Account/ | accessdate = 6 August 2012 | network = [[BBC]] | station = [[BBC World Service|World Service]] | date = 22 June 2012 }}</ref>

In 2014, Steare was appointed Visiting Professor of European Studies at the [[College of Europe]], Bruges.<ref name="CoE">{{cite web|url=http://whoswho.coleurope.eu/w/Roger.Steare|title=College of Europe - Roger Steare|work=[[College of Europe]]|accessdate=10 May 2015}}</ref> He is a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Arts]].<ref name="respublica" /><ref name="specialistspeakers" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://scy.co.uk/events/roger-steare-business-ethics-lecture |title=Roger Steare Business Ethics Lecture |publisher=SCY |date=9 February 2011 |accessdate=17 December 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.qfinance.com/business-ethics-viewpoints/the-morals-of-moneyhow-to-build-a-sustainable-economy-and-financial-sector?page=1 |title=The Morals of Money—How to Build a Sustainable Economy and Financial Sector |publisher=Qfinance |date=19 January 2010 |accessdate=17 December 2011}}</ref>

Steare has developed programs in leadership, ethics and corporate responsibility for organisations including [[BP]],<ref name="Hill" /> [[Citigroup]],<ref name="Poole">{{cite web | url = http://www.gordonpoole.com/Artists/Roger-Steare-(4).aspx |title = Roger Steare &#124; Corporate Philosopher &#124; Keynote Speaker |publisher=Gordonpoole.com |accessdate=17 December 2011}}</ref> [[HSBC]],<ref name="Hill" /> PwC,<ref name="Poole" /><ref name="PWC">{{cite web|url=http://www.ukmediacentre.pwc.com/News-Releases/PwC-brings-in-corporate-ethics-guru-Roger-Steare-as-an-adviser-1267.aspx|title=PricewaterhouseCoopers Media Centre – PwC brings in corporate ethics guru Roger Steare as an adviser|date=20 June 2012|publisher=[[PricewaterhouseCoopers]]|accessdate=6 August 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130104160636/http://www.ukmediacentre.pwc.com/News-Releases/PwC-brings-in-corporate-ethics-guru-Roger-Steare-as-an-adviser-1267.aspx|archive-date=4 January 2013|df=dmy-all}}</ref> the Financial Services Authority<ref name = "Smith" /> and the [[Serious Fraud Office (United Kingdom)|Serious Fraud Office]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sfo.gov.uk/about-us/our-views/director's-speeches/speeches-2011/the-institute-of-business-ethics.aspx |title=The Institute of Business Ethics &#124; About us &#124; SFO – Serious Fraud Office |publisher=SFO |date=25 February 2011 |accessdate=17 December 2011}}</ref>

Following the [[Deepwater Horizon oil spill]] in 2010, BP incorporated Steare's ethicability RIGHT framework for ethical decision-making into the BP 2011 Code of Conduct.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bp.com/liveassets/bp_internet/globalbp/STAGING/global_assets/downloads/C/Code_of_Conduct_2011.pdf|title=BP|website=Bp.com}}</ref>

The [[Financial Times]] profiled Steare in 2012<ref>{{cite news |title=Roger Steare, Cass Business School |url=https://www.ft.com/content/fd360472-c5b6-11e1-a5d5-00144feabdc0 |work=[[Financial Times]] |date=5 July 2012}}</ref> and has more than once cited his definition of corporate culture as "the way human beings behave together — what they value and what they celebrate".<ref name="Hill" /><ref name="Martin">{{cite news |last1=Martin |first1=Kevin |title=How to future-proof company culture |url=https://www.ft.com/content/39db7e82-3947-11ea-ac3c-f68c10993b04 |accessdate=18 March 2020 |work=Financial Times |date=13 February 2020}}</ref> In March 2018, Steare was featured in ''[[The Guardian]]'' in an article profiling the role of philosophers in business.<ref name="Tickle">{{cite news|last1=Tickle|first1=Louise|last2=Burke|first2=Claire|title=I work therefore I am: why businesses are hiring philosophers|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business-to-business/2018/mar/29/i-work-therefore-i-am-why-businesses-are-hiring-philosophers|accessdate=21 April 2018|work=the Guardian|date=29 March 2018 }}</ref> As of 2024, he is working at the ''[[Financial Times]]{{'}}'' Headspring Executive Development.<ref>{{cite web |title=Future of AI Summit 2024 Agenda - FT Live Event |url=https://ai.live.ft.com/agenda/speakers/3341090 |publisher=Financial Times |access-date=16 October 2024 }}</ref>
